- Equity-linked instruments: warrants expired February 11, 2026 (10-Q page:14); convertible notes were settled in 2025. The June 30, 2026 balance sheet shows long-term debt only through the term loan lines (10-Q page:2, page:18).

- Largest customer: one Network Partner, named as "Progressive Casualty Insurance", accounted for 27% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, all in the Insurance segment (10-K page:12). The 10-Q does not repeat the percentage for 2026 in the pages read; the 2026 concentration is Not supplied.

facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: the audited FY2025 statements and three unaudited interim periods (March 31, 2026, June 30, 2026, plus September 30, 2025 for the prior-year comparison) cover discrete quarters, six-month and nine-month year-to-date columns, three segments, issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA and variable marketing margin, and the single facility's carrying value. The Q2 10-Q reconciles segment profit to pre-tax income (page:21) and net income to Adjusted EBITDA (page:38), so non-GAAP add-backs can be traced to filed GAAP lines. - Strongest contrary evidence and limitation: the facility terms exist only as summaries. The 10-K states the covenant as "a first lien net leverage ratio of 5.00 to 1.00" tested "only if the loans and certain other obligations under the 2025 Revolving Facility exceed $20.0 million" (page:145), and the 10-Q states only that "The Company was in compliance with all covenants at June 30, 2026" (page:19). Evidence leads to a source risk: the definition of first lien net leverage, its EBITDA add-backs and the credit agreement baskets are not in the pack. The consequence is that a downstream module can describe the test and the compliance statement but cannot verify headroom or restricted-payment capacity. - Second source risk: the term-loan rate label. The 10-Q says borrowings "bear interest based on the Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") of 7.89%" (page:19) while the 10-K pricing is a spread over Term SOFR of 4.50%, or 4.25% after a Moody's rating condition achieved in January 2026 (page:145). The label may be an all-in rate, not the benchmark alone. Downstream modules must quote it as printed and flag the ambiguity. - Third source risk: management narrative versus filing. The July 29, 2026 release states an outlook for 2026 and the third quarter (page:3); the 10-Q does not. These are attributed management claims, forward-looking and unaudited, and cannot override filed figures. - Fourth source risk: a large tax-related swing in FY2025 net income. The 10-K statement of operations shows "Income tax benefit (expense) 130,284" against pre-tax income of "21,024" (page:110), and the fourth quarter release says the benefit reduced the full valuation allowance (page:1). Downstream modules must separate net income from operating results. - What cannot proceed from these sources alone: covenant headroom against the credit agreement definitions, guarantor-level analysis, letter of credit availability under the revolver, rating-agency analysis, market-price or valuation analysis, and anything after July 30, 2026. - Next evidence action: obtain the August 21, 2025 Credit Agreement (listed as exhibit 10.39, incorporated from the Form 8-K filed August 21, 2025, 10-K page:161), exhibit 21.1, any filing or release dated after July 30, 2026 including a third quarter 2026 10-Q and release, and the 2026 proxy statement.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Twelve-month revenue to June 30, 2026 was US$1,268.2m and Adjusted EBITDA US$153.6m, against US$132.9m in FY2025; cash interest paid over the same twelve months was US$34.7m; FY2025 net income was US$151.3m. The financial base is usable and shows a business that has grown quickly and cut leverage, with one facility, no maturity other than scheduled amortization before August 21, 2030 and a large undrawn revolver. On issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA, total debt to EBITDA moved from 4.56x at December 31, 2024 to 3.00x at December 31, 2025 and 2.58x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026; net debt to EBITDA moved from 3.54x to 2.39x and 1.86x. Revenue grew 24.1% in FY2025 and 30.8% in H1 2026, and Adjusted EBITDA grew 36.8% in H1 2026, but only 10.6% in Q2 2026 and it fell 16.3% from Q1 2026 (calculation C2). Cash interest paid was covered 4.42x for the last twelve months. Free cash flow for that period was US$73.9m. The restrictions are definitional rather than about data volume. Adjusted EBITDA excludes non-cash compensation and litigation settlements, so the same debt on unadjusted EBITDA is 3.10x total debt to EBITDA for the twelve months to June 30, 2026. Second-quarter 2026 variable marketing margin and Adjusted EBITDA were both below the first quarter, and the business depends on variable advertising spend and one large insurance partner. All leverage figures here use the principal of the 2025 Term Loan, not the carrying value net of issuance costs.

facts.label: Definition review
facts.text: - Adjusted EBITDA: net income excluding interest, income tax, amortization and depreciation, and further excluding non-cash compensation, non-cash impairment charges, gain or loss on disposals, gain or loss on investments, restructuring and severance, litigation settlements and contingencies, acquisition and disposition items, LendingTree Foundation contributions, dividend income, and one-time items (10-Q Q2 2026 page:37). "For the periods presented below, there are no adjustments for one-time items." - Size of the add-backs. FY2025 non-cash compensation added back was 29,202, litigation 15,661, restructuring 1,633, loss on investments 1,225, and dividend income of (4,223) was deducted (10-K page:96). Non-cash compensation was about 22.0% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA and 12.0% of H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA (calculation C9). The sensitivity that treats LTM non-cash compensation of 23,632 as a cost gives total debt to EBITDA of 3.05x and net debt to EBITDA of 2.20x (calculation C9). - Variable marketing expense is defined as advertising and promotional expense and excludes overhead and personnel costs. The 10-Q states "advertising and promotional expenses are equivalent to the non-GAAP measure variable marketing expense" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:30). Variable marketing margin is revenue less that expense (10-Q Q2 2026 page:35). - Net leverage as stated by management at December 31, 2025, 2.4x against 3.5x a year earlier, agrees with the computation here (release Q4 2025 page:2; calculation C5). The release does not print the formula, so agreement is observed, not confirmed by definition. - The covenant's first lien net leverage ratio, its EBITDA definition and the cash netting rules are in the credit agreement, which is not supplied. No covenant headroom is computed.

facts.label: Leverage
facts.text: Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.56x at December 31, 2024 to 3.00x at December 31, 2025 and 2.58x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026. Two things drove the FY2025 fall. Total principal fell by 75,682, because 115,307 of 2025 Notes were repaid in cash while bank debt rose by 39,625, from 359,375 to 399,000 (calculation C4). Adjusted EBITDA rose from 104,113 to 132,887. The LTM fall since December 31, 2025 comes from higher EBITDA (153,639 against 132,887) and a 2,000 term loan repayment. The covenant level of 5.00 to 1.00 first lien net leverage is above every Adjusted EBITDA-based ratio computed here, but its definition sits in an unsupplied agreement, so the two are not comparable. The unadjusted EBITDA view is 3.10x total debt to EBITDA at LTM June 30, 2026 against 4.46x at FY2025.

facts.label: Cash flow quality
facts.text: Free cash flow was 51,038 in FY2024, 60,680 in FY2025 and 73,877 over the last twelve months, which is about 48.1% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA (calculation C7). Three items qualify it. First, H1 2026 operating cash flow bore two of three equal instalments of a US$19.0m settlement. Second, working capital is large and seasonal: accounts receivable rose from 110,582 to 149,287 between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 while accounts payable rose from 6,735 to 47,351, and the 10-Q cash flow shows a 39,186 receivables outflow in H1 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:4). Third, FY2025 net income of 151,308 includes a 130,284 income tax benefit that is mostly deferred (deferred income taxes of (129,751) in the cash flow, 10-K page:111); cash taxes paid were only 1,772. The deferred tax asset was 124,867 at December 31, 2025 and 114,737 at June 30, 2026, and the 10-Q says certain option expiries could reverse part of it (10-Q Q2 2026 page:18).

facts.label: Data quality
facts.text: - Conflict: release versus 10-K balance sheet. The Q4 2025 release shows December 31, 2025 "Prepaid and other current assets 49,053", "Total current assets 240,708" and "Other non-current assets 5,522" (release Q4 2025 page:5). The audited 10-K shows 38,053, 229,708 and 16,522, plus equity investments of 475 (10-K page:110). The 10-Q Q2 2026 comparative agrees with the 10-K (page:2). The difference is 11,000 moved between current and non-current assets; total assets of 855,692 agree. The 10-K controls. Affected value: current assets and any current ratio at December 31, 2025. Downstream effect: use 229,708. - Reclassification: the Q2 10-Q states that "Certain prior period amounts have been reclassified" (page:6). The 10-Q shows December 31, 2025 other non-current assets of 16,997 against the 10-K split of 16,522 and 475 (equity investments). No reconciliation is printed. - Rate label: the 10-Q says borrowings "bear interest based on the Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") of 7.89%" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:19), 8.22% at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:144). The pricing is Term SOFR plus 4.50% or 4.25% (10-K page:145), so these appear to be all-in rates. Not confirmed by the sources. - Cross-check: the sum of the quarterly figures reconciles to the FY2025 totals for revenue and Adjusted EBITDA (calculation C14). The sum of the term loan gross principal less issuance costs and discount equals the carrying value at June 30, 2026 (calculation C4). - Extraction: text only; no image or XBRL fidelity review.

facts.label: Definition risks and key gaps
facts.text: - Adjusted EBITDA is issuer-defined and drives every leverage and cover ratio in the chart tables. The unadjusted ratios are shown beside them for that reason. - Covenant definitions, borrower and guarantor names and letters of credit under the revolver need the credit agreement, which is Not supplied (CP-0 gap, carried forward). - Nothing after July 30, 2026 is supplied. The 2026 outlook (revenue of US$1.30 to US$1.32 billion, Adjusted EBITDA of US$145 to US$152 million) is an attributed management claim from the July 29, 2026 release (release Q2 2026 page:3) and is not used in any ratio. - Concentration: one Network Partner, Progressive Casualty Insurance, was 27% of FY2025 revenue, all in Insurance (10-K page:12). The Insurance segment was 63.7% of FY2025 revenue and 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue (calculation C11); the 2026 share for the partner is Not supplied. - Variable marketing expense was 70.8% of H1 2026 revenue and 72.1% of Q2 2026 revenue (calculation C11). The 10-Q says the operating model is "highly sensitive to the amount and efficiency of variable marketing expenditures" (page:35) and expects "advertising costs to remain elevated for the remainder of 2026" (page:35).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: LendingTree is a US online marketplace that matches consumers with lenders, insurers and other providers and is paid fees by those providers, mostly when a consumer request is delivered. It is a public company with no sponsor or controlling owner identified in the supplied sources. The business has three reportable segments, Home, Consumer and Insurance, and its recent growth has come from Insurance, where earnings depend on carriers' advertising budgets and on the cost of the online media LendingTree buys to attract consumers. The creditor-relevant structure is simple: one first lien credit facility, secured on substantially all assets and guaranteed by material domestic subsidiaries, no dividend in over ten years, no share repurchases in 2024, 2025 or the first half of 2026, and no pending acquisition or ownership transaction in the supplied documents. The main uncertainties are the concentration in Insurance and in one carrier, the loss of the founder in October 2025 with his heirs holding a substantial stake, a weaker Q2 2026 against the company's own guidance, and the absence of the credit agreement. Everything after July 30, 2026 is Not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No acquisition, disposal, sponsor transaction or capital markets issue is described in any pinned document after the refinancing, so the transaction record is one financing event and a set of earlier changes; any transaction after July 30, 2026 is Not supplied. The refinancing is dated August 21, 2025, status closed. LendingTree entered into the 2025 Credit Agreement, a US$475.0 million first lien facility made up of a US$75.0 million revolving facility and a US$400.0 million term loan, both maturing August 21, 2030 (10-K page:144; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:18, page:39). The use of proceeds, as the filings state it, was to refinance the 2021 Credit Facility and the 2024 Term Loan, which collectively had US$402.8 million outstanding, with the US$400.0 million term loan and cash on hand at par plus accrued and unpaid interest, and for working capital and general corporate purposes (10-K page:97, page:144). The repayments were US$242.5 million of the 2021 term loan and US$160.3 million of the 2024 term loan; the 2021 revolver was terminated (10-K page:148). The company recognised a loss on extinguishment of US$7.9 million, incurred financing costs of US$8.6 million on the term loan of which about US$0.8 million was expensed, and paid US$3.9 million of original issue discount (10-K page:97, page:146). Earlier, the 0.50% Convertible Senior Notes due July 15, 2025, issued in July 2020 for US$575.0 million, were reduced by repurchases and the remaining US$95.3 million was repaid in cash at maturity on July 15, 2025, so no convertible debt, hedge or warrant remains and the warrants expired on February 11, 2026 (10-K page:142, page:144; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:14). The 2025 Term Loan is secured by substantially all assets including 100% of the equity in certain domestic subsidiaries and 65% of the voting equity of certain foreign subsidiaries, and guaranteed on a senior basis by material domestic subsidiaries; the revolver carries a US$30.0 million letter of credit sublimit; the financial covenant is a first lien net leverage ratio of 5.00 to 1.00 tested only when revolver usage exceeds US$20.0 million; and incremental capacity is the greater of US$58.0 million and 50% of consolidated EBITDA plus an unlimited amount subject to first lien net leverage of 3.10 to 1.00 (10-K page:145, page:146). Pricing is Term SOFR plus 4.50%, or 4.25% once a Moody's corporate family rating of B2 (stable) or better was achieved, which the 10-K says happened in January 2026; a 1.0% soft call premium applied during the first six months after closing (10-K page:145, page:146). The term loan balance was US$397.0 million at July 30, 2026 with no revolver borrowings and US$75.0 million available (10-Q Q2 2026 page:39, page:40). The liquidity effect, from CP-1, is cash of US$110.8 million and an undrawn US$75.0 million revolver at June 30, 2026, before any letters of credit, which are Not supplied. Sponsor and use-of-proceeds distributions: none documented; there is no sponsor and no distribution in the pinned sources. Which entity is the borrower, which subsidiaries guarantee and the exact covenant definitions are Not supplied because the credit agreement, exhibit 10.39 incorporated from a Form 8-K filed August 21, 2025, is not in the pack (10-K page:161).

facts.label: Ownership and control
facts.text: - Control rights: no controlling shareholder is documented. Anti-takeover provisions include blank-check preferred of up to 5,000,000 shares, no cumulative voting, board-only filling of vacancies and board sizing, board-called special meetings and no action by written consent (10-K page:69). Documentary Fact. - Founder and heirs: the founder, Doug Lebda, died on October 12, 2025 and his death was announced on October 13, 2025; before it he owned about 18%, and his "heirs and successors collectively hold a substantial portion of our outstanding shares" and "would have substantial voting control" if they acted collectively (10-K page:37, page:68). The estate or heirs' individual holdings and any voting arrangement are Not supplied. Insufficient Information on the exact percentage after his death. - Unnamed large holder: the 10-K cover assumes "a single stockholder who owned in excess of 20% of the voting common stock" is an affiliate (page:2); the holder is not named and the relationship to the estate is not stated. Insufficient Information; the 2026 proxy statement would normally name it. - Prior ownership: acquired by IAC/InterActiveCorp in May 2003 and spun off in August 2008 (10-K page:16). The exhibit list includes an assignment agreement of November 2, 2017 involving Liberty USA Holdings, LLC and a registration rights agreement of August 20, 2008 with Liberty Media Corporation (10-K page:158); the current status of that holder is Not supplied. - Dividend recapitalisation history: none documented. The company states no cash dividend in over ten years (10-K page:70).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: revenue is fees per delivered consumer request (10-K page:12) and Insurance was 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue (CP-1). Risk mechanic: carriers set advertising budgets by underwriting results, and the 10-Q says carriers "are broadly experiencing strong automotive underwriting results" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:24), so Insurance revenue is cyclical in carrier profitability and in rate competition; contracts for Home lenders can be terminated for convenience (10-K page:12). Credit implication: debt service capacity rests on one segment's demand cycle with no contracted revenue, so leverage tolerance should assume Insurance can reverse faster than fixed costs. Counter-evidence: the three segments have different cycles, and Insurance segment profit grew 25% in Q2 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:31). No logged conflict counters this. 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: variable marketing expense was 70.8% of H1 2026 revenue (CP-1) and management expects advertising costs to stay elevated (10-Q Q2 2026 page:35). Risk mechanic: media cost rising faster than monetisation compresses variable marketing margin before fixed costs, and the Q2 2026 variable marketing margin was 87.3 against 99.5 in Q1 2026 (CP-1). Credit implication: margin resilience is the key monitoring item, since Adjusted EBITDA for the covenant and for CP-1 leverage rests on it. 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: Progressive Casualty Insurance was 27% of FY2025 revenue (10-K page:12), which on the rounded percentage is about 42.4% of Insurance revenue (calculation C3). Risk mechanic: a carrier can cut its budget at short notice, and QuoteWizard's own risk factors list "concentration of customers with large insurance carriers" (10-K page:27). Credit implication: a single relationship change could move Adjusted EBITDA materially; the contract terms and the 2026 share are Not supplied, so the exposure cannot be sized for 2026. Counter-evidence: in FY2024 two partners together supplied 33%, so concentration has shifted between names, not fallen. 4. Sponsor and governance alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, no dividend in over ten years, no repurchases since at least January 1, 2024 (10-K page:70, page:78), a CEO succession on October 13, 2025 and heirs holding a substantial stake (10-K page:37, page:68). Risk mechanic: alignment is with public equity holders and a family estate whose intentions are not documented; a block of that size can influence board composition or a sale. Credit implication: no creditor-adverse behaviour is documented, but willingness cannot be tested without the credit agreement's restricted payment terms; a change of control provision, if any, is Not supplied. 5. Key uncertainties. The credit agreement, the 2026 proxy statement, the 2026 concentration, the unnamed 20% holder and anything after July 30, 2026. Credit implication: monitoring posture should treat leverage as improving on reported numbers but unverified against covenant definitions.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: LendingTree is a moderate credit that is improving, with leverage now low for a high yield issuer but earnings that are volatile and concentrated. The strongest support is the balance sheet: USD 110.8 million of cash, an undrawn USD 75.0 million revolver, one facility maturing August 21, 2030 and USD 73.9 million of free cash flow over the last twelve months. The weakest point is earnings quality and concentration: Adjusted EBITDA adds back non-cash compensation, Insurance is 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue, one partner supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue, and management lowered its 2026 outlook. What decides the outcome is whether carrier advertising budgets and media costs hold; the credit agreement, which is not supplied, would show how much protection the covenants give.

### Financial base view

Twelve-month revenue to June 30, 2026 was US$1,268.2m and Adjusted EBITDA US$153.6m, against US$132.9m in FY2025; cash interest paid over the same twelve months was US$34.7m; FY2025 net income was US$151.3m. The financial base is usable and shows a business that has grown quickly and cut leverage, with one facility, no maturity other than scheduled amortization before August 21, 2030 and a large undrawn revolver. On issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA, total debt to EBITDA moved from 4.56x at December 31, 2024 to 3.00x at December 31, 2025 and 2.58x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026; net debt to EBITDA moved from 3.54x to 2.39x and 1.86x. Revenue grew 24.1% in FY2025 and 30.8% in H1 2026, and Adjusted EBITDA grew 36.8% in H1 2026, but only 10.6% in Q2 2026 and it fell 16.3% from Q1 2026 (calculation C2). Cash interest paid was covered 4.42x for the last twelve months. Free cash flow for that period was US$73.9m. The restrictions are definitional rather than about data volume. Adjusted EBITDA excludes non-cash compensation and litigation settlements, so the same debt on unadjusted EBITDA is 3.10x total debt to EBITDA for the twelve months to June 30, 2026. Second-quarter 2026 variable marketing margin and Adjusted EBITDA were both below the first quarter, and the business depends on variable advertising spend and one large insurance partner. All leverage figures here use the principal of the 2025 Term Loan, not the carrying value net of issuance costs.

### Definition review

- Adjusted EBITDA: net income excluding interest, income tax, amortization and depreciation, and further excluding non-cash compensation, non-cash impairment charges, gain or loss on disposals, gain or loss on investments, restructuring and severance, litigation settlements and contingencies, acquisition and disposition items, LendingTree Foundation contributions, dividend income, and one-time items (10-Q Q2 2026 page:37). "For the periods presented below, there are no adjustments for one-time items."

- Size of the add-backs. FY2025 non-cash compensation added back was 29,202, litigation 15,661, restructuring 1,633, loss on investments 1,225, and dividend income of (4,223) was deducted (10-K page:96). Non-cash compensation was about 22.0% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA and 12.0% of H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA (calculation C9). The sensitivity that treats LTM non-cash compensation of 23,632 as a cost gives total debt to EBITDA of 3.05x and net debt to EBITDA of 2.20x (calculation C9).

- Variable marketing expense is defined as advertising and promotional expense and excludes overhead and personnel costs. The 10-Q states "advertising and promotional expenses are equivalent to the non-GAAP measure variable marketing expense" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:30). Variable marketing margin is revenue less that expense (10-Q Q2 2026 page:35).

- Net leverage as stated by management at December 31, 2025, 2.4x against 3.5x a year earlier, agrees with the computation here (release Q4 2025 page:2; calculation C5). The release does not print the formula, so agreement is observed, not confirmed by definition.
- The covenant's first lien net leverage ratio, its EBITDA definition and the cash netting rules are in the credit agreement, which is not supplied. No covenant headroom is computed.
### Leverage

Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.56x at December 31, 2024 to 3.00x at December 31, 2025 and 2.58x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026. Two things drove the FY2025 fall. Total principal fell by 75,682, because 115,307 of 2025 Notes were repaid in cash while bank debt rose by 39,625, from 359,375 to 399,000 (calculation C4). Adjusted EBITDA rose from 104,113 to 132,887. The LTM fall since December 31, 2025 comes from higher EBITDA (153,639 against 132,887) and a 2,000 term loan repayment. The covenant level of 5.00 to 1.00 first lien net leverage is above every Adjusted EBITDA-based ratio computed here, but its definition sits in an unsupplied agreement, so the two are not comparable. The unadjusted EBITDA view is 3.10x total debt to EBITDA at LTM June 30, 2026 against 4.46x at FY2025.
### Coverage

Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.73x in FY2024, 3.57x in FY2025 and 4.42x over the last twelve months. Net interest expense was 10,402 in Q2 2025 and 8,483 in Q2 2026. H1 2025 interest expense was split across three instruments (US$11.3m on the 2021 credit agreement, US$7.8m on the 2024 Term Loan and US$0.6m on the 2025 Notes), against US$16.8m on the single 2025 Credit Agreement in H1 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:19). The sources give no further driver. FY2025 interest expense includes a loss on repayment of term loans of 7,861 that is not a cash interest cost. Interest paid in 2025 straddles two debt structures, so FY2025 cover is a mixed-basis figure.
### Cash flow quality

Free cash flow was 51,038 in FY2024, 60,680 in FY2025 and 73,877 over the last twelve months, which is about 48.1% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA (calculation C7). Three items qualify it. First, H1 2026 operating cash flow bore two of three equal instalments of a US$19.0m settlement. Second, working capital is large and seasonal: accounts receivable rose from 110,582 to 149,287 between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 while accounts payable rose from 6,735 to 47,351, and the 10-Q cash flow shows a 39,186 receivables outflow in H1 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:4). Third, FY2025 net income of 151,308 includes a 130,284 income tax benefit that is mostly deferred (deferred income taxes of (129,751) in the cash flow, 10-K page:111); cash taxes paid were only 1,772. The deferred tax asset was 124,867 at December 31, 2025 and 114,737 at June 30, 2026, and the 10-Q says certain option expiries could reverse part of it (10-Q Q2 2026 page:18).
### Liquidity

Liquidity at June 30, 2026 was cash of 110,766 plus an undrawn revolver of 75,000, or 185,766 before any letters of credit (calculation C10). At December 31, 2025 it was 156,073 on the same basis. Only 4,000 of debt falls due within twelve months of June 30, 2026. The revolver matures on August 21, 2030, the same date as the term loan, so there is no revolver maturity ahead of the term loan. The issuer states that it expects cash and operating cash flow "to be sufficient to fund our operating needs for the next twelve months and beyond" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:39).
### Data quality

- Conflict: release versus 10-K balance sheet. The Q4 2025 release shows December 31, 2025 "Prepaid and other current assets 49,053", "Total current assets 240,708" and "Other non-current assets 5,522" (release Q4 2025 page:5). The audited 10-K shows 38,053, 229,708 and 16,522, plus equity investments of 475 (10-K page:110). The 10-Q Q2 2026 comparative agrees with the 10-K (page:2). The difference is 11,000 moved between current and non-current assets; total assets of 855,692 agree. The 10-K controls. Affected value: current assets and any current ratio at December 31, 2025. Downstream effect: use 229,708.

- Reclassification: the Q2 10-Q states that "Certain prior period amounts have been reclassified" (page:6). The 10-Q shows December 31, 2025 other non-current assets of 16,997 against the 10-K split of 16,522 and 475 (equity investments). No reconciliation is printed.

- Rate label: the 10-Q says borrowings "bear interest based on the Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") of 7.89%" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:19), 8.22% at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:144). The pricing is Term SOFR plus 4.50% or 4.25% (10-K page:145), so these appear to be all-in rates. Not confirmed by the sources.

- Cross-check: the sum of the quarterly figures reconciles to the FY2025 totals for revenue and Adjusted EBITDA (calculation C14). The sum of the term loan gross principal less issuance costs and discount equals the carrying value at June 30, 2026 (calculation C4).
- Extraction: text only; no image or XBRL fidelity review.
### Definition risks and key gaps
- Adjusted EBITDA is issuer-defined and drives every leverage and cover ratio in the chart tables. The unadjusted ratios are shown beside them for that reason.
- Covenant definitions, borrower and guarantor names and letters of credit under the revolver need the credit agreement, which is Not supplied (CP-0 gap, carried forward).

- Nothing after July 30, 2026 is supplied. The 2026 outlook (revenue of US$1.30 to US$1.32 billion, Adjusted EBITDA of US$145 to US$152 million) is an attributed management claim from the July 29, 2026 release (release Q2 2026 page:3) and is not used in any ratio.

- Concentration: one Network Partner, Progressive Casualty Insurance, was 27% of FY2025 revenue, all in Insurance (10-K page:12). The Insurance segment was 63.7% of FY2025 revenue and 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue (calculation C11); the 2026 share for the partner is Not supplied.

- Variable marketing expense was 70.8% of H1 2026 revenue and 72.1% of Q2 2026 revenue (calculation C11). The 10-Q says the operating model is "highly sensitive to the amount and efficiency of variable marketing expenditures" (page:35) and expects "advertising costs to remain elevated for the remainder of 2026" (page:35).
## Calculations
All inputs are printed amounts in US$ thousands from the locators given above. Ratios are rounded to two decimals in the tables and to three decimals here.
**C1. LTM amounts (FY2025 plus H1 2026 less H1 2025).**
- Variable marketing margin: 346,644 + 186,886 − 161,375 = 372,155.
**C2. Growth rates.**
**C3. Unadjusted EBITDA = net income + interest expense, net + income tax expense (benefit) + depreciation + amortization of intangibles.**
**C4. Debt and cash.**
- Gross principal FY2024: 2025 Notes 115,307 + current bank 10,313 + long-term bank 349,062 = 474,682 (bank debt 359,375).
- Tie-out, June 30, 2026: 397,000 − issuance costs (34 + 3,307) − discount (34 + 3,342) = 397,000 − 6,717 = 390,283, equal to the carrying value.
**C5. Leverage ratios.**
- Management cross-check: release Q4 2025 states net leverage of 2.4x at year-end 2025 and 3.5x at year-end 2024; the computed 2.392 and 3.536 round to the same figures.
**C6. Coverage.**
**C7. Free cash flow and cash conversion.**
- LTM operating cash flow: 73,103 + 40,717 − 27,743 = 86,077. LTM capital expenditures: 12,423 + 5,935 − 6,158 = 12,200. LTM free cash flow: 86,077 − 12,200 = 73,877.
- LTM free cash flow / LTM Adjusted EBITDA: 73,877 / 153,639 = 48.1%.
**C9. Add-back sensitivity.**
- Non-cash compensation share of Adjusted EBITDA: FY2025 29,202 / 132,887 = 22.0%; H1 2026 9,264 / 77,171 = 12.0%.
- LTM non-cash compensation add-back: 29,202 + 9,264 − 14,834 = 23,632.
- Adjusted EBITDA less non-cash compensation: 153,639 − 23,632 = 130,007. Total debt / that figure: 397,000 / 130,007 = 3.054. Net debt / that figure: 286,234 / 130,007 = 2.202.
**C10. Liquidity.** June 30, 2026: 110,766 + 75,000 = 185,766. December 31, 2025: 81,073 + 75,000 = 156,073. Letters of credit are Not supplied and are not deducted.
**C11. Mix and spend ratios.**
- Insurance share of total segment profit: FY2025 174,417 / 352,047 = 49.5%; Q2 2026 49,997 / 88,823 = 56.3%.
**C12. Discrete Q2 derivations (H1 less Q1).**
- Inputs: Q1 2026 operating cash flow 11,552 and Q1 2025 (210) (10-Q Q1 2026 page:3); Q1 capital expenditures 2,770 and 3,414 and interest paid 8,018 and 8,828 (10-Q Q1 2026 page:4).

**C13. Working capital movement.** Accounts receivable June 30, 2026 less December 31, 2025: 149,287 − 110,582 = 38,705. Accounts payable: 47,351 − 6,735 = 40,616. Accrued contingencies: 13,001 − 863 = 12,138 reduction.
**C14. Quarter sums.**
- Q4 2025 net income cross-check: 151,308 − (−3,513) − 10,165 = 144,656, equal to the release.
**C15. Balance sheet difference between release and 10-K.** 240,708 − 229,708 = 11,000 current assets; 16,522 + 475 − (5,522 + 475) = 11,000 non-current assets.

### Business and transaction view

LendingTree is a US online marketplace that matches consumers with lenders, insurers and other providers and is paid fees by those providers, mostly when a consumer request is delivered. It is a public company with no sponsor or controlling owner identified in the supplied sources. The business has three reportable segments, Home, Consumer and Insurance, and its recent growth has come from Insurance, where earnings depend on carriers' advertising budgets and on the cost of the online media LendingTree buys to attract consumers. The creditor-relevant structure is simple: one first lien credit facility, secured on substantially all assets and guaranteed by material domestic subsidiaries, no dividend in over ten years, no share repurchases in 2024, 2025 or the first half of 2026, and no pending acquisition or ownership transaction in the supplied documents. The main uncertainties are the concentration in Insurance and in one carrier, the loss of the founder in October 2025 with his heirs holding a substantial stake, a weaker Q2 2026 against the company's own guidance, and the absence of the credit agreement. Everything after July 30, 2026 is Not supplied.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition, disposal, sponsor transaction or capital markets issue is described in any pinned document after the refinancing, so the transaction record is one financing event and a set of earlier changes; any transaction after July 30, 2026 is Not supplied. The refinancing is dated August 21, 2025, status closed. LendingTree entered into the 2025 Credit Agreement, a US$475.0 million first lien facility made up of a US$75.0 million revolving facility and a US$400.0 million term loan, both maturing August 21, 2030 (10-K page:144; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:18, page:39). The use of proceeds, as the filings state it, was to refinance the 2021 Credit Facility and the 2024 Term Loan, which collectively had US$402.8 million outstanding, with the US$400.0 million term loan and cash on hand at par plus accrued and unpaid interest, and for working capital and general corporate purposes (10-K page:97, page:144). The repayments were US$242.5 million of the 2021 term loan and US$160.3 million of the 2024 term loan; the 2021 revolver was terminated (10-K page:148). The company recognised a loss on extinguishment of US$7.9 million, incurred financing costs of US$8.6 million on the term loan of which about US$0.8 million was expensed, and paid US$3.9 million of original issue discount (10-K page:97, page:146). Earlier, the 0.50% Convertible Senior Notes due July 15, 2025, issued in July 2020 for US$575.0 million, were reduced by repurchases and the remaining US$95.3 million was repaid in cash at maturity on July 15, 2025, so no convertible debt, hedge or warrant remains and the warrants expired on February 11, 2026 (10-K page:142, page:144; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:14). The 2025 Term Loan is secured by substantially all assets including 100% of the equity in certain domestic subsidiaries and 65% of the voting equity of certain foreign subsidiaries, and guaranteed on a senior basis by material domestic subsidiaries; the revolver carries a US$30.0 million letter of credit sublimit; the financial covenant is a first lien net leverage ratio of 5.00 to 1.00 tested only when revolver usage exceeds US$20.0 million; and incremental capacity is the greater of US$58.0 million and 50% of consolidated EBITDA plus an unlimited amount subject to first lien net leverage of 3.10 to 1.00 (10-K page:145, page:146). Pricing is Term SOFR plus 4.50%, or 4.25% once a Moody's corporate family rating of B2 (stable) or better was achieved, which the 10-K says happened in January 2026; a 1.0% soft call premium applied during the first six months after closing (10-K page:145, page:146). The term loan balance was US$397.0 million at July 30, 2026 with no revolver borrowings and US$75.0 million available (10-Q Q2 2026 page:39, page:40). The liquidity effect, from CP-1, is cash of US$110.8 million and an undrawn US$75.0 million revolver at June 30, 2026, before any letters of credit, which are Not supplied. Sponsor and use-of-proceeds distributions: none documented; there is no sponsor and no distribution in the pinned sources. Which entity is the borrower, which subsidiaries guarantee and the exact covenant definitions are Not supplied because the credit agreement, exhibit 10.39 incorporated from a Form 8-K filed August 21, 2025, is not in the pack (10-K page:161).

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: revenue is fees per delivered consumer request (10-K page:12) and Insurance was 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue (CP-1). Risk mechanic: carriers set advertising budgets by underwriting results, and the 10-Q says carriers "are broadly experiencing strong automotive underwriting results" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:24), so Insurance revenue is cyclical in carrier profitability and in rate competition; contracts for Home lenders can be terminated for convenience (10-K page:12). Credit implication: debt service capacity rests on one segment's demand cycle with no contracted revenue, so leverage tolerance should assume Insurance can reverse faster than fixed costs. Counter-evidence: the three segments have different cycles, and Insurance segment profit grew 25% in Q2 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:31). No logged conflict counters this.

2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: variable marketing expense was 70.8% of H1 2026 revenue (CP-1) and management expects advertising costs to stay elevated (10-Q Q2 2026 page:35). Risk mechanic: media cost rising faster than monetisation compresses variable marketing margin before fixed costs, and the Q2 2026 variable marketing margin was 87.3 against 99.5 in Q1 2026 (CP-1). Credit implication: margin resilience is the key monitoring item, since Adjusted EBITDA for the covenant and for CP-1 leverage rests on it.

3. Concentration risk. Evidence: Progressive Casualty Insurance was 27% of FY2025 revenue (10-K page:12), which on the rounded percentage is about 42.4% of Insurance revenue (calculation C3). Risk mechanic: a carrier can cut its budget at short notice, and QuoteWizard's own risk factors list "concentration of customers with large insurance carriers" (10-K page:27). Credit implication: a single relationship change could move Adjusted EBITDA materially; the contract terms and the 2026 share are Not supplied, so the exposure cannot be sized for 2026. Counter-evidence: in FY2024 two partners together supplied 33%, so concentration has shifted between names, not fallen.

4. Sponsor and governance alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, no dividend in over ten years, no repurchases since at least January 1, 2024 (10-K page:70, page:78), a CEO succession on October 13, 2025 and heirs holding a substantial stake (10-K page:37, page:68). Risk mechanic: alignment is with public equity holders and a family estate whose intentions are not documented; a block of that size can influence board composition or a sale. Credit implication: no creditor-adverse behaviour is documented, but willingness cannot be tested without the credit agreement's restricted payment terms; a change of control provision, if any, is Not supplied.

5. Key uncertainties. The credit agreement, the 2026 proxy statement, the 2026 concentration, the unnamed 20% holder and anything after July 30, 2026. Credit implication: monitoring posture should treat leverage as improving on reported numbers but unverified against covenant definitions.

**C1. Segment shares (from CP-1 calculation C11).** Insurance share of revenue: FY2025 711,880 / 1,117,324 = 63.7%; Q2 2026 209,263 / 313,422 = 66.8%. Variable marketing expense / revenue, H1 2026: 453,803 / 640,689 = 70.8%.

**C2. Guidance versus Q2 2026 actual (US$ millions).** Adjusted EBITDA: guided range 38 to 40; reported 35.162 (35,162 thousands); shortfall to the low end 38 − 35.162 = 2.838. Variable marketing margin: guided 93 to 97; reported 87.339; shortfall to the low end 93 − 87.339 = 5.661. Revenue guided 305 to 325; reported 313.4, inside the range. Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guide of 145 to 152 less H1 2026 of 77.171 implies second-half Adjusted EBITDA of 67.829 to 74.829. Net leverage tie-out at March 31, 2026: principal 394,000 + 4,000 = 398,000 less cash 85,518 = 312,482; trailing Adjusted EBITDA 132,887 + 42,009 − 24,626 = 150,270; 312,482 / 150,270 = 2.08x against the CFO's statement of 2.1x (release Q1 2026 page:1).

**C3. Progressive share of Insurance revenue (rounded input).** 27% × 1,117,324 = 301,677 (thousands); 301,677 / 711,880 = 42.4%. The 27% is a rounded percentage, so the result is approximate to about plus or minus 0.5 percentage points of revenue. Analyst Interpretation. FY2024: 22% + 11% = 33% of revenue.
**C4. Debt repaid in the refinancing.** 242.5 + 160.3 = 402.8 (US$ millions), equal to the "collectively had $402.8 million outstanding" (10-K page:97, page:148).

## Request

LendingTree, Inc. (issuer id `tree`), as of 2026-11-05 on the `credit_snapshot` pathway, with an information cutoff of 2026-11-05. This module synthesises the fundamental credit view from the accepted financial base and the business and transaction context, in USD. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-07-29_tree-63026xer.htm.jsonl | b737e26fe71071d22f2d669bce2532cab38eb1e5741e87f2852ff6a85cf82520 | Pinned release; reached through the upstream handoffs |
| context | d200051bbc093266762c46db0da57fcc23aae21f45bdfa41362781dff2cb6e7d | User run settings; not issuer evidence |
| Handoff module | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | c84ab10531b22ca79243cab80e778b189c7ae85ab40d1bc94cfa4d4426e74643 | Source readiness and gap list; limitations carried into the gaps below |
| CP-1 | 66d19075d0cda548fb908b11cbace236ac80961fccbfe892b5468b6b2cd9a36f | Financial base: statements, leverage, cover, liquidity and maturities; the basis for every financial figure here |

| CP-1A | 27aa6bb2d2a88e25a00702feb3dd400595805f473712abaaf922df6d060d8625 | Business, ownership, governance, transaction, timeline, conflicts and outlook history; the basis for every business claim here |

The evidence is upstream only: figures are those of CP-1 and CP-1A, whose locators (`page:N` in the pinned files) they carry. Short forms: 10-K (FY2025), 10-Q Q2 2026, release Q2 2026. New arithmetic is in `## Calculations`. The pinned files were searched only for hedging, derivative and interest-rate-exposure terms (10-K page:105, 10-Q Q2 2026 page:40).
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| LendingTree's credit profile has strengthened: total debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.56x to 2.58x and liquidity is USD 185.8 million, but earnings are concentrated in Insurance and one partner, and the quality of EBITDA is unverified. | Medium | The credit agreement is not supplied, so covenant headroom, guarantors and letter of credit usage are unverified, and nothing after July 30, 2026 is included. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.56x at December 31, 2024 to 2.58x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026. | Leverage tolerance has improved, but the ratio uses issuer-defined EBITDA; treating non-cash compensation as a cost gives 3.05x. | Medium |

| Cash was USD 110.8 million and the USD 75.0 million revolver was undrawn at June 30, 2026, against USD 4.0 million due within twelve months. | Near-term liquidity risk is low; the next large maturity is August 21, 2030. | High |

| Cash interest paid was USD 34.7 million over twelve months, covered 4.42x; free cash flow was USD 73.9 million. | Debt service is well covered at current earnings; interest floats, and each 100 basis points costs about USD 4.0 million a year. | High |

| Insurance was 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue, one partner supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue, and Q2 2026 results fell below April guidance. | Earnings depend on carrier advertising budgets and media costs, so a downturn in either would reduce EBITDA before costs adjust. | Medium |

| Goodwill and intangibles are 45.7% of total assets and tangible equity is negative USD 96.3 million. | Protection for creditors rests on enterprise value and therefore on earnings durability, since hard assets are limited. | High |
### Credit view

LendingTree is a moderate credit that is improving, with leverage now low for a high yield issuer but earnings that are volatile and concentrated. The strongest support is the balance sheet: USD 110.8 million of cash, an undrawn USD 75.0 million revolver, one facility maturing August 21, 2030 and USD 73.9 million of free cash flow over the last twelve months. The weakest point is earnings quality and concentration: Adjusted EBITDA adds back non-cash compensation, Insurance is 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue, one partner supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue, and management lowered its 2026 outlook. What decides the outcome is whether carrier advertising budgets and media costs hold; the credit agreement, which is not supplied, would show how much protection the covenants give.
### Key findings

First, LendingTree has deleveraged materially. Total debt principal fell from USD 474.7 million at December 31, 2024 to USD 397.0 million at June 30, 2026, and Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 153.6 million for the twelve months to June 30, 2026, so total debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.56x to 2.58x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA from 3.54x to 1.86x [CP-1]. Management's statement of net leverage of 2.4x at year-end 2025 agrees with the 2.39x computed here [CP-1, CP-1A].

Second, the improvement depends on the EBITDA definition. Adjusted EBITDA excludes non-cash compensation, which was about 22.0% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, and litigation settlements; on EBITDA built from net income, interest, tax, depreciation and amortization the same debt is 3.10x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 and 4.46x for FY2025 [CP-1]. The credit agreement's own EBITDA definition is not supplied, so covenant leverage cannot be computed.

Third, liquidity is strong and the maturity profile is clear. Cash was USD 110.8 million, the USD 75.0 million revolver had no borrowings, and only USD 4.0 million of the term loan falls due within twelve months; the final maturity of both facilities is August 21, 2030 [CP-1, CP-1A]. The financial covenant is a first lien net leverage ratio of 5.00 to 1.00 that is tested only when revolver usage exceeds USD 20.0 million, so with the revolver undrawn the term loan lenders have no routine maintenance test; this is the issuer's own summary, not a reading of the agreement [CP-1, CP-1A].

Fourth, earnings are sensitive to a single segment and a single partner. Insurance was 63.7% of FY2025 revenue and 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue; Progressive Casualty Insurance supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue, about 42.4% of Insurance revenue on the rounded percentage [CP-1A]. Variable marketing spend was 70.8% of H1 2026 revenue, and variable marketing margin fell to 29.2% of revenue in H1 2026 from 33.8% in FY2024 [CP-1].

Fifth, momentum has softened. Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 35.2 million was 16.3% below Q1 2026 and below the USD 38 to 40 million guided in April, variable marketing margin was USD 87.3 million against a USD 93 to 97 million guide, and management cut its full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA outlook to USD 145 to 152 million from USD 152 to 162 million [CP-1, CP-1A]. These outlooks are management claims.

Sixth, cash generation is good and interest is largely floating. Free cash flow was USD 73.9 million over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, about 48.1% of Adjusted EBITDA, after cash interest of USD 34.7 million [CP-1]. The term loan bears interest at Term SOFR plus 4.50% or 4.25%; the sources disclose no hedge, so a 100 basis point rise would cost about USD 4.0 million a year, 5.4% of LTM free cash flow (calculation P2).

Seventh, ownership and capacity for creditor-adverse action are not testable. There is no sponsor, no dividend in over ten years and no repurchase in 2024, 2025 or the first half of 2026, which is supportive behaviour; the founder died in October 2025, his heirs collectively hold a substantial stake, and incremental debt capacity under the facility is the greater of USD 58.0 million and 50% of consolidated EBITDA plus an unlimited amount if first lien net leverage does not exceed 3.10 to 1.00 [CP-1A]. On issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA the ratio-based part alone could allow roughly USD 190.0 million of additional first lien net debt, illustrative only because the agreement's EBITDA definition is not supplied (calculation P5).
### Strengths and weaknesses

**Strength, deleveraging and cash conversion (Documentary Fact).** LendingTree cut total debt principal by USD 77.7 million (16.4%) between December 31, 2024 and June 30, 2026 while growing Adjusted EBITDA, and capital spending was 0.96% of LTM revenue, which leaves most operating cash flow available for debt service [CP-1]. The mechanism is a low-capital marketplace model whose costs are mostly variable advertising, so cash conversion is high when demand is stable.

**Strength, liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact).** Cash of USD 110.8 million plus an undrawn USD 75.0 million revolver is USD 185.8 million, about 46.4 times the USD 4.0 million due within twelve months, and no maturity other than scheduled amortization falls before August 21, 2030 [CP-1]. This removes near-term refinancing risk and gives time for the earnings base to prove durable.

**Strength, creditor-friendly behaviour so far (Analyst Interpretation).** The company has paid no cash dividend in over ten years, repurchased no shares in 2024, 2025 or the first half of 2026 despite a USD 96.7 million authorization, repaid its convertible notes in cash at maturity, and has no identified sponsor [CP-1A]. Behaviour is documented, but legal capacity depends on the credit agreement, which is not supplied.

**Strength, diversified segments and flexible cost base (Management Language, qualified).** Management says it adjusts selling and marketing spend dynamically with partner demand; the three segments respond to different cycles, although Insurance was 49.5% of FY2025 segment profit and 56.3% in Q2 2026 [CP-1A] (10-Q Q2 2026 page:30 for management's statement). This is management's characterisation; the Q2 2026 results show the flex is partial, as variable marketing margin fell while revenue grew.

**Weakness, earnings quality and definitions (Documentary Fact).** Adjusted EBITDA is issuer-defined and drives every leverage and cover ratio; add-backs include non-cash compensation of USD 29.2 million in FY2025 [CP-1]. Treating LTM non-cash compensation as a cost raises total debt to EBITDA from 2.58x to 3.05x, so the deleveraging is real but flattered, and covenant EBITDA may differ from either measure.

**Weakness, concentration (Documentary Fact).** Insurance was 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue and one carrier supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue, with two carriers at 22% and 11% in FY2024 [CP-1A]. Carriers set advertising budgets by their own underwriting results and can cut them quickly, so a budget cut reduces revenue at once while the speed of the cost response is not documented in the sources.

**Weakness, margin pressure and a weaker Q2 (Documentary Fact).** Variable marketing margin was 27.9% of revenue in Q2 2026 against 33.4% in Q2 2025, Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was below guidance, and management expects advertising costs to stay elevated [CP-1, CP-1A]. If media costs keep rising faster than partner fees, cash flow weakens while the debt stays fixed at USD 397.0 million.

**Weakness, floating-rate debt and thin hard-asset cover (Documentary Fact).** The term loan is floating, no hedge is disclosed, and goodwill and intangibles are 45.7% of total assets with negative tangible equity of USD 96.3 million (calculation P6). Creditor protection therefore depends on enterprise value rather than hard assets, which is a mechanic and not a recovery conclusion.

**Weakness, governance transition and untested protections (Insufficient Information).** The founder died in October 2025, the CEO changed on October 13, 2025, and the heirs hold a substantial, unquantified stake; a single holder above 20% is not named [CP-1A]. The credit agreement, proxy statement and any change of control terms are not supplied, so restricted payment capacity, guarantor coverage and the effect of an ownership change on tax attributes are unknown.
### Credit assessment
| Dimension | View | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Business risk | Moderate: transactional marketplace revenue, three segments, concentration in Insurance and in one carrier | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A operating model, customer concentration and credit translations |

| Financial risk | Improving: total debt to Adjusted EBITDA 2.58x, net 1.86x, cover 4.42x; 3.05x if non-cash compensation is a cost | Documentary Fact for the ratios; Analyst Interpretation for the view | Medium | CP-1 leverage, cover and definition review |
| Liquidity | Strong: USD 185.8 million before letters of credit; USD 4.0 million due within twelve months | Documentary Fact | High | CP-1 liquidity and maturity tables |
| Governance and creditor control | Supportive behaviour to date; protections untested | Analyst Interpretation | Low | CP-1A governance table; credit agreement not supplied |

| Overall fundamental credit view | Moderate credit, improving, with earnings that are volatile and concentrated | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | All of the above; confidence is below High because the credit agreement and later events are not supplied |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Insurance advertising cycle and carrier concentration | Carriers set budgets from underwriting results; one carrier supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue; revenue is per delivered request with no contracted minimum in the sources | A budget cut reduces revenue before media spend is cut, lowering EBITDA and raising leverage against fixed debt | Material |

| Earnings quality and definition | Adjusted EBITDA adds back non-cash compensation and litigation; covenant definition unknown | Reported leverage of 2.58x may understate leverage on a stricter basis (3.05x or 3.10x) | Material |

| Margin compression from media costs | Variable marketing is 70.8% of H1 2026 revenue; advertising costs expected to stay elevated; margin down to 29.2% of revenue from 33.8% | Cash flow available for debt service falls faster than revenue in a weak quarter | Material |

| Covenant and debt capacity | Single springing covenant on the revolver; incremental first lien capacity; restricted payment terms unknown | Creditors could face additional first lien debt or distributions the sources neither confirm nor exclude | Material |
| Floating-rate exposure | Term Loan at Term SOFR plus a margin; no hedge disclosed | Each 100 basis points costs about USD 4.0 million a year | Minor |

| Founder succession and ownership concentration | CEO changed October 13, 2025; heirs hold a substantial stake; unnamed 20% holder | Possible board, strategy or ownership change; ownership changes can limit tax attributes | Minor |

| Regulatory and litigation | Heavily regulated lead generation; a USD 19.0 million TCPA class settlement was paid in instalments through Q2 2026 | Settlement and compliance costs can reduce cash flow; accruals were USD 0.9 million at June 30, 2026 | Minor |

| Refinancing | Final maturity August 21, 2030 for both facilities; USD 393.0 million of the term loan due after twelve months | Refinancing exposure is distant but depends on the earnings base then | Minor |
## Calculations

All inputs are printed amounts or accepted figures from the upstream handoffs, in US dollars in thousands unless a unit is given. Other derived figures are those of CP-1 (leverage, cover, free cash flow, liquidity, margins) and CP-1A (mix, guidance, concentration).

**P1. EBITDA sensitivity of total debt to EBITDA.** LTM Adjusted EBITDA 153,639 and total debt principal 397,000 at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). If EBITDA falls 10%: 397,000 / (153,639 × 0.9) = 2.871x. 20%: 397,000 / (153,639 × 0.8) = 3.230x. 30%: 397,000 / (153,639 × 0.7) = 3.691x. 40%: 397,000 / (153,639 × 0.6) = 4.307x. The fall in EBITDA that would raise total debt to EBITDA to 5.00x is 1 − 397,000 / (5 × 153,639) = 48.3%. This is a ratio on issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA, not the covenant, whose definition and net basis are not supplied.

**P2. Interest-rate sensitivity.** 1% × 397,000 = 3,970 a year (the 10-Q states USD 4.0 million, 10-Q Q2 2026 page:40). As a share of LTM free cash flow of 73,877: 3,970 / 73,877 = 5.4%. Interest cover if EBITDA halves: 153,639 × 0.5 = 76,820; 76,820 / 34,740 = 2.21x on LTM cash interest paid.
**P3. Free cash flow after scheduled amortization.** 73,877 − 4,000 = 69,877. Cash build in H1 2026: 110,766 − 81,073 = 29,693.
**P4. Debt reduction.** 474,682 − 397,000 = 77,682; 77,682 / 474,682 = 16.4%. Liquidity coverage of near-term debt: 185,766 / 4,000 = 46.4 times.

**P5. Illustrative first lien incremental capacity.** 3.10 × 153,639 = 476,281; less net debt of 286,234 = 190,047, about USD 190.0 million. The term in the agreement is a first lien net leverage test on consolidated EBITDA as defined in the credit agreement, which is not supplied; the figure uses issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA and total net debt, includes no netting rules and is not a capacity estimate.

**P6. Asset composition.** Goodwill 381,539 + intangible assets, net 35,516 = 417,055; 417,055 / total assets 911,631 = 45.7%. Tangible equity: 320,772 − 417,055 = −96,283. Deferred income tax assets of 114,737 are a further 12.6% of total assets (114,737 / 911,631).
**P7. Capital intensity.** LTM capital expenditures 12,200 / LTM revenue 1,268,169 = 0.96%.

**P8. Guidance arithmetic.** From CP-1A: full-year Adjusted EBITDA guide 145 to 152 (USD millions) less H1 2026 of 77.171 implies second-half 67.829 to 74.829; Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 35.162 was 2.838 below the low end of the 38 to 40 guide.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters and what it affects | Severity | Action |

| 2025 Credit Agreement not supplied: covenant EBITDA definition, borrower and guarantor entities, restricted payments, incremental debt, change of control, letters of credit | Limits any statement on covenant headroom, creditor control and capacity for adverse action; lowers confidence below High | Material | Supply the agreement and compliance disclosure |

| Nothing after July 30, 2026, including Q3 2026 results and any current reports | The credit view is stale relative to the November 5, 2026 cutoff; guidance was already lowered once | Material | Supply later filings |
| 2026 proxy statement, holder list, unnamed 20% holder and heirs' arrangements not supplied | Ownership control and succession cannot be assessed | Minor | Supply the definitive proxy statement |
| Partner contracts and 2026 largest-partner share not supplied | Cannot size the 2026 Insurance concentration or termination rights | Material | Supply later disclosure |

| Hedging: none disclosed in the sources searched | The floating-rate exposure is taken as unhedged, but a hedge elsewhere cannot be excluded | Minor | Confirm in the credit agreement or later filings |
| Annual maturity split of the USD 393.0 million long-term portion not printed | Only the current portion and the final maturity are known | Minor | Use as printed |

| Upstream conflicts logged, not reconciled: release versus 10-K balance sheet classification; valuation allowance wording | Affects current assets at December 31, 2025 and the description of the tax benefit; the 10-K controls | Minor | Use the 10-K; keep the conflict open |
| Text extraction only; no XBRL or image review | Small risk of table misreads | Minor | Check against the filed HTML |
| Upstream status: CP-0 verdicts were READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all consumers; CP-1 and CP-1A carry the gaps above | The synthesis is restricted accordingly | Minor | Carry the limitations |
## Next module

- CP-5: trace each claim in the key findings and the strengths and weaknesses to the upstream locators; keep the two logged conflicts open; treat the outlook as management claims; do not read the illustrative incremental capacity as an estimate.
- Report assembly: present the credit view as moderate and improving, with confidence Medium, and state the missing credit agreement and the post-July 30, 2026 gap where they change a conclusion.
